title: The symmetric quotient and Rees presentation of the ordinary blowup
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ a quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $b:B=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ be the ordinary glued blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Write $\mathcal R=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal I^n$ for the quasi-coherent sheaf Rees algebra [def-nagata-sheaf-rees-algebra], with $\mathcal R_0=\mathcal O_T$, and $\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)$ for the quasi-coherent symmetric algebra [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra], graded by symmetric degree [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. The degree-one inclusion induces a canonical surjective degree-preserving morphism of graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebras $q:\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I)\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal R$ whose degree-zero map is the identity. On every affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, with $I=\Gamma(V,\mathcal I)$, there are canonical graded identifications $\Gamma(V,\mathcal R)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n$ and $\Gamma(V,\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal I))=\operatorname{Sym}_A(I)$; in particular $\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^n)=I^n$. Under these identifications, $q_V$ is surjective and sends $x_1\cdots x_n\in\operatorname{Sym}^n_A(I)$ to $x_1\cdots x_n\in I^n$. There is a canonical isomorphism $e:B\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal R)$ over $T$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Its restriction over every affine $V$ is the identification of both schemes with $\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{n\ge0}I^n)$, and these identifications commute with the restriction maps on affine refinements, namely coefficientwise localization of the Rees algebras.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-rees-symmetric-presentation] to $T,\mathcal I$. It supplies the canonical $\varphi$, the affine symmetric-algebra identification, $\Gamma(V,\mathcal I^n)=I^n$, and the graded coefficient identification $\theta_V$ with the polynomial Rees ring. Identify that ring with $\bigoplus_n I^n$ by $\sum_n a_nt^n\mapsto(a_n)_n$; its inverse is $(a_n)_n\mapsto\sum_n a_nt^n$. Both expressions have finite support, and the convolution formula for polynomial multiplication is precisely the product on the direct sum, so these are inverse graded algebra maps. Set $q=\varphi$. The cited statement gives degree preservation, identity in degree zero, degreewise affine surjectivity and the displayed monomial formula. Taking the finite sum of homogeneous preimages gives surjectivity of $q_V$ on the whole algebra; affine opens cover $T$, so this also proves surjectivity as a sheaf morphism. The same cited coefficient formulas give compatibility with affine restrictions.

proof.text: Choose the affine cover $(V_i)$ used in the ordinary blowup. By [def-nagata-global-blowup-local-model] and [def-nagata-affine-blowup], its local schemes are $\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal R_{A_i}(I_i))$. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists], the relative Proj restricts over $V_i$ to $\operatorname{Proj}(\Gamma(V_i,\mathcal R))$. Step 1 identifies their graded rings, including the degree-zero structural maps, and hence identifies these local schemes over $V_i$. Here the identification on homogeneous prime ideals is inverse image under the coefficient isomorphism, and on the structure sheaf it sends each equal-degree fraction $a/f^k$ to the fraction with the same coefficients; this is exactly the Proj construction of [def-nagata-affine-proj].

source.place: Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine), first assertion and proof; Constructions Tag 01NQ (lemma-glue-relative-proj)

proof.text: Check the transitions, rather than just the local schemes. The relative-Proj transitions are induced by graded restriction [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction], with the chart formulas specified in [def-nagata-relative-proj]. On $D(s)\subset V_i$ Step 1 makes this $a_nt^n\mapsto(a_n/1)t^n$. This is the coefficient map $\rho_s$ of [def-nagata-rees-localization-map], and [def-nagata-affine-blowup-restriction-map] defines a map to the base-change fibre product from precisely this map. Compose it with the first projection to compare maps into the original blowup. The tensor-product version $\rho_s$ is viewed as an $A$-algebra map by $a\mapsto1\otimes a$. The resulting map agrees with the relative-Proj restriction on the charts below, so [lem-nagata-proj-affine-restriction] identifies its image with the restricted open and supplies its inverse there. On a standard Proj chart both thus act on equal-degree fractions by $a/f^k\mapsto(a/1)/(f/1)^k$. Cover $V_i\cap V_j$ by opens principal in both affines using [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both]. On each such open the two overlap isomorphisms are the same composite $r_{j,s}\circ r_{i,s}^{-1}$, the explicit definition of [def-nagata-global-blowup-overlap-basic-map]. Equality on the whole overlap follows from uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing]. Thus the identifications of Step 2 intertwine the full overlap maps of [def-nagata-global-blowup-glue-data]. No intersection of affines has been assumed affine.

By [def-nagata-global-blowup], $B$ is the scheme glued from the ordinary datum. Step 3 says that the local identifications into $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal R)$ agree on its overlaps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $e$ and, to the inverse local identifications, a map in the other direction. The two composites restrict to identities on their respective open covers, so uniqueness in the same lemma makes them identities. The structural maps agree on the cover as well, so $e$ lies over $T$. To check any affine $V$, enlarge the original affine cover by $V$. The ordinary glued model for this cover identifies with $B$ by [prop-nagata-global-blowup-cover-independent], with identity comparison on common affine refinements. The relative-Proj chart identifications are cover-independent by [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. Repeating the same local comparison on this enlarged cover therefore gives $e$ again, since it agrees on the original cover. Its restriction over $V$ is the coefficient identification of Step 2. Further affine restrictions commute because the coefficient maps in Step 1 do; on principal refinements they are exactly the localization maps checked in Step 3. This proves all the asserted compatibility and canonicity.

lean.statement: theorem blowup_rees_symmetric_presentation {T : Scheme.{u}} (I : T.IdealSheafData) : ∃ hqc : I.toModules.IsQuasicoherent, ∃ q : (@SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData T I.toModules hqc ⟶ I.reesData), (∀ U : T.affineOpens, Function.Surjective (q.app U)) ∧ (∀ (U : T.affineOpens) (n : ℕ) (x : Fin n → Γ(I.toModules, U.1)), (reesAlgebra (I.ideal U)).subtype (q.app U (∏ i, SymmetricAlgebra.ι (T.presheaf.obj (op U.1)) (I.toModules.val.obj (op U.1)) (x i))) = Polynomial.monomial n (∏ i, @id (T.presheaf.obj (op U.1)) (I.toModulesι.app U.1 (x i)))) ∧ (∀ U : T.affineOpens, Function.Bijective (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.sectionMap I.toModules (op U.1))) ∧ (∀ (U : T.affineOpens) (n : ℕ), Set.range (fun x : Γ((I ^ n).toModules, U.1) ↦ @id (T.presheaf.obj (op U.1)) ((I ^ n).toModulesι.app U.1 x)) = (↑((I.ideal U) ^ n) : Set (T.presheaf.obj (op U.1)))) ∧ (∀ (U : T.affineOpens) (F : reesAlgebra (I.ideal U)) (n : ℕ), (reesGradingEquivPow (I.ideal U) n ((DirectSum.decomposeAlgEquiv (reesGrading (I.ideal U)) F) n) : T.presheaf.obj (op U.1)) = (F : Polynomial (T.presheaf.obj (op U.1))).coeff n) ∧ I.relProjReesIso.inv ≫ I.reesData.relProjHom = I.blowupMap ∧ (∀ U : T.affineOpens, I.blowupι U ≫ I.relProjReesIso.inv = I.reesData.relProjι U) ∧ (∀ (U V : T.affineOpens) (h : U ≤ V), I.blowupFunctor.map (homOfLE h) ≫ I.blowupι V ≫ I.relProjReesIso.inv = I.reesData.relProjFunctor.map (homOfLE h) ≫ I.reesData.relProjι V) ∧ (∀ (U V : T.affineOpens) (h : U ≤ V) (F : reesAlgebra (I.ideal V)), (reesAlgebra (I.ideal U)).subtype (I.reesData.res h F) = (F : Polynomial (T.presheaf.obj (op V.1))).map (T.presheaf.map (homOfLE (X := T.Opens) h).op).hom)
